rated_messages.input_message: See what it is like to let the urge pass. You can have an urge and choose not to smoke.
Take a deep breath and let it out slowly. Notice that you are completely OK for this one breath. Do it again.
Some people find that having a simple mantra can really help, especially if things feel stressful. Try repeating something simple to yourself like: "I can do it!".
You spent a long time training your brain to want a cig. Now you're retraining your brain, and it's natural that this might take time.
Take a deep breath. Focus on today and the things you have accomplished. How many urges have you let pass? Give yourself some credit!
If this situation becomes stressful for you, make an excuse to leave for a few minutes. If this doesn't help, it might be better to just leave early.
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.

Now is a good time for BREAKS B=stop and Brake R=Read how your body feels E=Expand and take deep breaths A=Allow everything to be as it is K=Know what's important to you S=take 1 Step in a direction important to you

Did you know that just seeing other people smoke activates a part of your brain that is connected with the action of you smoking? This can bring on strong urges to smoke. One simple solution is to avoid seeing others smoke.

If you find yourself thinking: "I can't do this", "I need a cig", or "I'll just have one", make sure you tell yourself "I absolutely CAN do this", "I'm in control". Take control of your negative thoughts!
